extraction.name: MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark
extraction.description: MVBench is a comprehensive Multi-modal Video understanding Benchmark designed to evaluate the comprehension capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs), particularly their temporal understanding in dynamic video tasks. It covers 20 challenging video tasks that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame. The benchmark uses a novel static-to-dynamic method to define temporal-related tasks, transforming static tasks into dynamic ones requiring a broad spectrum of temporal skills. It automatically converts public video annotations into multiple-choice QA for evaluation, ensuring fairness with ground-truth annotations and minimizing manual intervention.
extraction.creator: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao
extraction.publisher: Shanghai AI Laboratory, Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, The University of Hong Kong, Fudan University, State Key Laboratory for Novel Software Technology, Nanjing University
extraction.citeAs: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao. MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark. arXiv:2311.17005, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The MVBench dataset is created by defining 20 temporal-related tasks using a novel static-to-dynamic method, adapting static image tasks with dynamic evolution. Public video annotations from 11 diverse video benchmarks (STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, TVQA) are then automatically converted into multiple-choice Question Answering (QA) format using Large Language Models (LLMs), specifically ChatGPT, to evaluate each task.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos from 11 public datasets: STAR [82], PAXION [79], Moments in Time V1 [57], FunQA [87], CLEVRER [95], Perception Test [61], Charades-STA [20], MoVQA [102], NTU RGB+D [48], VLN-CE [32], and TVQA [35].
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos were selected from existing benchmarks based on three criteria: (1) Video Diversity: 11 video datasets covering a broad spectrum of domains and scenes (first-person to third-person, indoor to outdoor) were chosen. (2) Temporal Sensitivity: Short clips with negligible motions and extremely long videos with overly complicated contexts were eliminated, selecting videos with intermediate durations (primarily 5s to 35s). (3) Question Difficulty: Selection criteria were designed for STAR (randomly shifting start/end points to increase complexity) and CLEVRER (excluding questions requiring more than 10 conditions) to balance difficulty.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multiple-choice QAs were automatically generated from open-sourced video annotations using LLMs. ChatGPT [58] was used to generate a question for each video based on task definitions. Answer options were created via two methods: (1) Template-Based Construction: For most tasks, options were directly constructed from ground truth annotations (e.g., correct action, opposite action, 'not sure' for Action Antonym; four directions and 'stationary' for Moving Direction). (2) LLM-Based Generation: For the Unexpected Action task, ChatGPT converted open-ended QAs into multiple-choice format with options. Answer options were randomly sampled (3 to 5 per question) and shuffled. LLMs were also used to ensure similar and reasonable text lengths for all options to prevent answer leakage bias.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Answer options were randomly sampled (3 to 5 per question) and shuffled to strengthen evaluation robustness. LLMs were used to guarantee that all answer options of a question are of similar and reasonable lengths, preventing the common issue of answer leakage where longer options tend to be correct.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: For cognition tasks such as egocentric navigation and episodic reasoning, visual information alone may not be sufficient, suggesting that the inclusion of other modalities like depth and audio could be beneficial for these tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating the comprehension capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs), specifically for benchmarking their temporal understanding skills in 20 challenging video tasks. It is used for training, testing, and validation of MLLMs, as demonstrated by the evaluation of various MLLMs on MVBench and the development of VideoChat2.
